title: A Winter for the Hymn
premise: Marguerite Almeida returns to the decaying Almeida house to bury their twin brother Mateus, only to learn at the funeral that the body in the casket is wearing Marguerite's own dental work. As the mirrors begin lagging a second behind reality, Marguerite realizes the family's inherited 'hymn'—a counting song sung by every Almeida before them—is not a lullaby but a summons, and that one twin was always meant to be given. With the count nearing its final verse and the reflection growing bolder each night, Marguerite must choose between protecting their niece Sol by surrendering themselves, or breaking the inheritance entirely. In the end, Marguerite shatters the great mirror mid-count, trading their own reflection for the family's freedom, and walks out of the house with no face in any glass—but alive, and finally visible.
about_author: Rafael Nakamura is the pen name of a former mortuary transcriptionist who spent six years recording final words in coastal New England funeral homes. Their fiction blends grief-ritual detail with slow-burn domestic horror.

chapters.title: The Wrong Casket
chapters.summary: Marguerite arrives home after fifteen years for Mateus's funeral and notices the corpse has their childhood chipped tooth. POV: Marguerite. Beat: dread disguised as grief; the wrongness is small but undeniable.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Aunt Iria lays out the old rules: cover mirrors at dusk, never sing past the third verse of the hymn. Marguerite pretends to comply while cataloguing exits. POV: Marguerite. Beat: claustrophobic return to a childhood of unspoken bargains.

chapters.title: Sol's Counting Song
chapters.summary: Nine-year-old niece Sol hums the hymn on the stairs, skipping verses she says 'the house doesn't like.' Marguerite corrects her and feels the walls listen. POV: Marguerite. Beat: protective instinct ignites against inherited silence.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Brushing teeth at midnight, Marguerite sees their reflection blink after they do. They test it with a raised hand; the lag holds. POV: Marguerite. Beat: private terror—the first proof the noises were never pipes.

chapters.title: The Funeral Portrait
chapters.summary: Reviewing funeral photos, Marguerite finds the open-casket shot shows an empty box with two shadows standing behind it. POV: Marguerite. Beat: grief curdles into investigation; Mateus may not be gone.

chapters.title: Iria's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite finds Aunt Iria's hidden ledger: every Almeida generation records which twin 'stayed.' The current page lists both names, neither crossed out. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the horror has bookkeeping; inheritance as predation.

chapters.title: What Mateus Told Me
chapters.summary: In a dream, Mateus stands in the hall mirror and warns: 'It counts twins so it can take one and keep one watching.' POV: Marguerite. Beat: ambiguous contact—warning or lure?

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: The mirror delay grows to three seconds; the reflection now finishes movements Marguerite abandoned. Iria rehangs sheets over every glass without being asked. POV: Marguerite. Beat: escalation; the house adapts faster than its people.

chapters.title: Sol Sees Him
chapters.summary: Sol tells Marguerite about 'Uncle in the wall' who sings harmony. She draws him with Marguerite's face. POV: alternating Marguerite/Sol. Beat: the child normalizes what adults deny; stakes become concrete.

chapters.title: Verse Four
chapters.summary: Marguerite researches the hymn in the parish archive and finds a fourth verse torn from every surviving hymnal—including theirs. POV: Marguerite. Beat: deliberate erasure; someone in the family cut the truth out.

chapters.title: Iria Confesses, Partly
chapters.summary: Iria admits the hymn is a contract: the house keeps the family safe and solvent in exchange for a voice every generation. She refuses to say what happens if payment fails. POV: Marguerite. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes—Iria chose comfort over honesty for decades.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Left
chapters.summary: Marguerite visits Dora Reyes, who fled the house in 1987. Dora reveals the fourth verse is a renunciation—one twin must refuse the inheritance aloud, inside the mirror room, at the winter solstice. POV: Marguerite. Beat: hope with a price tag; a map forms.

chapters.title: Reflections Without Owners
chapters.summary: Mirrors throughout town now show the Almeida house's empty rooms. The lag is spreading outward. POV: Marguerite. Beat: containment failing; the secret won't stay indoors.

chapters.title: Mateus's Room
chapters.summary: Marguerite searches Mateus's untouched bedroom and finds his journal: he'd been rehearsing the renunciation for months—he planned to break the cycle himself. POV: Marguerite. Beat: devastating reversal; the dead sibling was braver than the living one.

chapters.title: The House Sings Back
chapters.summary: At 3 a.m. the whole house hums the hymn in a voice like wet gravel. Every covered mirror bulges against its sheeting. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the entity drops pretense; the countdown becomes audible.

chapters.title: Count the Days
chapters.summary: Marguerite calculates the solstice: eleven days. Iria begins packing 'for a holiday,' still refusing to name the danger to Sol. POV: Marguerite. Beat: ticking clock formalized; family denial vs. survival.

chapters.title: Sol's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sol confesses the wall-Uncle promised her that if she learns all four verses, 'one of your family gets to stay forever.' She's been practicing. POV: Sol. Beat: heartbreak—the child has been groomed as the next instrument.

chapters.title: Burning the Hymnals
chapters.summary: Marguerite burns the family hymnals in the yard; the fire casts reflections in bare soil. That night, cold spots follow them room to room. POV: Marguerite. Beat: defiance provokes retaliation; no neutral ground remains.

chapters.title: Dora's Tape
chapters.summary: Dora sends a cassette: her grandmother singing the full fourth verse. Halfway through, a second voice joins from nowhere, and the tape warps. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the weapon exists but is contaminated; using it means exposure.

chapters.title: The Twin in the Glass
chapters.summary: The reflection stops mimicking and speaks: it claims to be the real Marguerite, left behind fifteen years ago when 'the other one' walked out. POV: Marguerite. Beat: identity crisis weaponized—which twin buried whom?

chapters.title: Fifteen Years Ago
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Marguerite flees the house after the solstice ritual, leaving Mateus mid-hymn, telling themselves the screams were wind. POV: Marguerite (past). Beat: guilt excavated; the lag began the night they ran.

chapters.title: Iria's Verse
chapters.summary: Cornered, Iria admits she was the 'kept' twin of her generation; her sister went into the mirror room in 1961 and never came out, and Iria has been paying interest ever since. POV: Marguerite/Iria. Beat: the villain is also a victim; inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: Marguerite moves Sol and Iria to a motel. The motel bathroom mirror shows the Almeida hallway. POV: Marguerite. Beat: false safety; distance is an illusion the house permits.

chapters.title: What the House Wants
chapters.summary: Through the glass, the reflection explains terms: one Almeida voice per generation, freely sung, or the house takes the whole line—and it considers Sol's practiced verses a binding offer. POV: Marguerite. Beat: negotiation with something that lies beautifully.

chapters.title: Testing the Reflection
chapters.summary: Marguerite sets traps—questions only they could answer. The reflection answers all correctly, then adds details Marguerite had forgotten, as if reading a deeper self. POV: Marguerite. Beat: epistemological horror; the enemy knows them better than they do.

chapters.title: Sol Runs Home
chapters.summary: Sol slips away at dawn and returns to the house to finish learning the song, believing she can save everyone by volunteering. POV: Sol. Beat: the child repeats the family's oldest mistake out of love.

chapters.title: The Mirror Room Opened
chapters.summary: Marguerite breaks into the sealed mirror room and finds generations of names scratched inside the glass—each pair of twins, one crossed out. Mateus's name is freshly scratched, uncrossed. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the ledger made flesh; Mateus may be held, not dead.

chapters.title: A Voice Through the Silver
chapters.summary: Inside the room, Marguerite hears Mateus faintly, singing off-key exactly as he did as a boy—a signal, not a haunting. He's alive in the lag between seconds. POV: Marguerite. Beat: rescue becomes possible; grief converts to mission.

chapters.title: Iria's Choice
chapters.summary: Iria offers herself to renew the contract and void Sol's accidental offer. Marguerite refuses to let another generation pay. They fight; Iria locks Marguerite in and drives toward the house alone. POV: Marguerite. Beat: loyalty weaponized against truth; the mentor tries to sacrifice herself.

chapters.title: Chasing Iria
chapters.summary: Marguerite races back through a snowstorm, mirrors along the route showing Iria's car arriving hours early—as if the road itself belongs to the house now. POV: Marguerite. Beat: pursuit through distorted geography; time bends near the solstice.

chapters.title: The Kept Twin
chapters.summary: Marguerite finds Iria at the threshold, hymn begun. Marguerite interrupts at verse three, and the house goes silent with attention. POV: Marguerite. Beat: standoff; the whole family in the mirror room's orbit.

chapters.title: Verse Four, Spoken
chapters.summary: Marguerite recites the renunciation from memory—refusing the inheritance for the entire line—but falters on the final word, and the reflection steps out of the glass wearing their face. POV: Marguerite. Beat: climax begins; courage incomplete, the cost named.

chapters.title: Two Marguerites
chapters.summary: The double argues its case: it stayed, it suffered, it deserves the life. Sol recognizes her true uncle-aunt by an old scar and says so aloud, anchoring Marguerite's identity. POV: Marguerite/Sol. Beat: identity resolved not by logic but by witnessed love.

chapters.title: Mateus's Hand
chapters.summary: From inside the mirror, Mateus grips the double's wrist—the kept twin holding the replacement—buying Marguerite the second needed to finish the verse. POV: Marguerite. Beat: sacrifice answered by sacrifice; the dead act for the living.

chapters.title: Shattering
chapters.summary: Marguerite completes the renunciation and drives a chair through the great mirror mid-count. The house screams in every voice it ever collected; the lag collapses to zero everywhere. POV: Marguerite. Beat: climax peak—destruction as liberation.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Glass
chapters.summary: Dawn. Every mirror in the house is blank silver. Marguerite appears in none of them—not cursed, just absent. Iria weeps; Sol asks if it hurts. 'Only when I look,' Marguerite says. POV: Marguerite. Beat: bittersweet victory; freedom with a permanent mark.

chapters.title: Burial, Corrected
chapters.summary: They rebury the casket properly, engraving both twins' names, and Mateus's scratched name inside the broken frame is found crossed out at last—released. POV: Marguerite. Beat: mourning finally accurate; rituals repaired.

chapters.title: Leaving the House Standing
chapters.summary: Instead of burning the house, Marguerite leaves it unlocked and empty, doors open—an inheritance refused rather than destroyed. Snow fills the halls. POV: Marguerite. Beat: thematic closure; breaking cycles means walking away, not erasing history.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Sol sends a photo of the three of them at the motel. In it, Marguerite casts no reflection in the window behind them—but is smiling more truly than in any picture before. POV: Sol. Beat: visibility redefined; love sees what glass cannot.

chapters.title: A Winter for the Hymn
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Marguerite, faceless in every mirror, teaches Sol a new song with no fourth verse and no count. Somewhere far off, a house stands silent under snow. POV: Marguerite. Beat: resolution—inheritance rewritten into choice; the hymn ends where the family begins.
